messages:
Maria Santos: heads up — customer reported flaky 408s and duplicate token refresh when app goes to background then back to foreground during uploads. stacktrace + logs attached.

AJ: ugh. do we have a simple repro app? sounds like cancellation -> retry -> authenticator race.

Maria Santos: minimal steps: 1) start large file upload using Retrofit suspend call, 2) press home, 3) re-open app within ~3s. sometimes request gets cancelled with java.io.EOFException, then our retry interceptor retries and triggers a token refresh twice -> second refresh fails with 401 and then we loop. log: 

```
2026-03-18 14:22:01.123 I/Upload: start upload
2026-03-18 14:22:05.456 I/Upload: onPause
2026-03-18 14:22:07.789 W/OkHttp: call canceled: /v1/upload
2026-03-18 14:22:07.790 D/RetryInterceptor: retrying call, attempt=1
2026-03-18 14:22:07.792 I/Auth: starting refresh token (id=abc123)
2026-03-18 14:22:07.800 D/RetryInterceptor: retrying call, attempt=2
2026-03-18 14:22:07.801 I/Auth: starting refresh token (id=def456)
2026-03-18 14:22:08.010 E/Server: 401 unauthorized
```

Maria Santos: client config: OkHttpClient with AuthInterceptor (adds header) + Authenticator to handle 401s. We also have a RetryInterceptor wrapping network calls.

Kai Park: classic. When a call is cancelled, OkHttp will sometimes produce a followup retry. If your retry logic triggers a token refresh on both the original and the followup, you'll do two refreshes.

AJ: are you using OkHttp Authenticator or an interceptor for token refresh? Authenticator is only called on 401 responses, interceptors get invoked for every request.

Maria Santos: interceptor adds auth header from TokenProvider.get(). Authenticator calls TokenProvider.refreshIfNeeded(). TokenProvider currently does a synchronized refresh but it's coroutine-based — we call it from both a blocking Authenticator path and from suspend interceptors which may not coordinate perfectly.

Sam L: We had something similar — solution was to centralize refresh behind a singleflight/mutex and use the Authenticator exclusively to trigger refresh on 401s; interceptors should just read cached token and not attempt refresh. Also be careful when cancelling: cancelled calls may not produce 401 but will cause your RetryInterceptor to clone and re-execute calls which can race the authenticator.

AJ: also check Dispatcher.maxRequestsPerHost and connection pool keepalive. If the app background->foreground causes a transient network tear-down, OkHttp may create a new call while the old one is cancelled, giving you the race.

Kai Park: small code pattern that helped us (Kotlin, coroutines):

```
private val refreshMutex = Mutex()
private var cachedToken: String? = null

suspend fun getToken(): String = cachedToken ?: run {
  refreshMutex.withLock {
    cachedToken ?: run {
      // perform network refresh synchronously here
      val new = refreshTokenNetworkCall()
      cachedToken = new
      new
    }
  }
}

// Authenticator (called on okhttp dispatcher thread)
override fun authenticate(route: Route?, response: Response): Request? {
  // block here waiting for the singleflight to finish, use a blocking bridge
  val token = runBlocking { tokenProvider.getTokenBlocking() }
  return response.request.newBuilder().header("Authorization", "Bearer $token").build()
}
```

Sam L: key point — provide a blocking getTokenBlocking() that uses the same mutex/singleflight as your coroutine path. otherwise you get two simultaneous refreshes.

Maria Santos: ok will try converting TokenProvider to offer both suspend and blocking flavors that share the same Mutex.

AJ: separate note — consider not retrying on CallCanceledException in your RetryInterceptor. If a call was canceled by the system because of app lifecycle, automatic retries may be wrong. Maybe only retry on network IOExceptions and not cancellations triggered by the dispatcher.

Maria Santos: good call. current RetryInterceptor checks "if (!call.isExecuted())" poorly. we'll add explicit check: if (e is java.io.InterruptedIOException && e.message?.contains("timeout") == true) then retry, but if call isCanceled then don't.

Kai Park: also add an SDK sample app that reproduces: foreground service -> start upload -> press home -> adb shell am start -a ... to reopen quickly. We should add test harness on CI run on emulator to catch regressions.

Maria Santos: created ticket #3421, pushing a PR to SDK with: 1) TokenProvider refactor (shared mutex + blocking entry), 2) RetryInterceptor skipping cancel-based retries, 3) added sampleapp repro and README with adb steps.

ci-bot: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/android-sdk/pull/987 — CI checks queued :github:  

AJ: :eyes: I'll review the TokenProvider changes. If we still see duplicate refreshes after that, we may need to move refresh entirely into Authenticator-only flow.

Maria Santos: thanks all, will update thread after validated with customer. :pray:
